question: A Magento developer ports a PHPUnit suite to xUnit. Two test classes add products to the same `static List<Product>` and assert on its count. The suite passes locally most of the time and fails at random in CI. What is the most likely cause?
options: xUnit reuses one instance of each test class for all its tests, so the list is never reset
xUnit runs separate test classes in parallel, so both change the static list at once
The CI agent runs tests in alphabetical order, which differs from the order on your machine
`List<T>` is a value type, so each test changes its own copy and the count drifts
explanation: Each test class is its own test collection, and collections run in parallel by default, so shared static state races. Instance reuse is the wrong explanation: xUnit creates a new instance of the class for every test, which is why instance fields are safe and static fields are not.

question: Where does per-test setup go in xUnit, the equivalent of PHPUnit's `setUp()`?
options: A method marked `[SetUp]`, which xUnit calls before each test
An override of `TestBase.Initialize()`, called before each test
The test class constructor, since each test gets a new instance
A class fixture, since xUnit builds it again before each test
explanation: The constructor runs before every test because every test gets a fresh instance, and `Dispose` runs after it. A class fixture is the opposite case: it is created once and shared by all tests in the class. `[SetUp]` is NUnit's attribute and does not exist in xUnit.

question: You want to test `ApplyDiscount(decimal price, int percentage)` with five `decimal` price rows. Which approach compiles and reports each row separately?
options: A `[Fact]` with a `foreach` loop that asserts on every row of an array
A `[Theory]` with `[InlineData(19.99m, 10, 17.991m)]` rows, one per price
A `[Theory]` with `[MemberData]` returning `TheoryData<decimal, int, decimal>`
Five separate `[Fact]` methods, each calling one shared assertion helper
explanation: Attribute arguments must be compile-time constants and `decimal` is not one, so `[InlineData]` cannot carry `decimal` literals. `[MemberData]` with a typed `TheoryData` can, and each row is reported as its own test. A `foreach` in one fact stops at the first failing row and hides which one broke.

question: Which test signature is a bug in xUnit v3?
options: `public async Task SaveAsync_ValidProduct_Persists()`
`public async ValueTask SaveAsync_ValidProduct_Persists()`
`public void Save_ValidProduct_PersistsToRepository()`
`public async void SaveAsync_ValidProduct_Persists()`
explanation: An `async void` test cannot be awaited by the runner, and xUnit v3 fails such tests at runtime. `Task` and `ValueTask` are both supported return types, and a synchronous `void` test is fine when the code under test is synchronous.

question: A test class loads a 50 MB fixture file in its constructor, and its 40 tests only read the data. What is the better design?
options: Keep it in the constructor so every test gets its own clean copy
Load it once in an `IAsyncLifetime` class shared via `IClassFixture<T>`
Keep it in a static field that the first test to run fills in
Merge the 40 tests into one test so the file loads only once
explanation: A class fixture is created once per class and injected into each test instance, which suits expensive, read-only setup; `IAsyncLifetime` lets it load the file asynchronously. A static field filled by the first test depends on test order and on parallel execution, the exact problem fixtures exist to avoid. One giant test loses the per-behavior reporting.

question: Your team installs the .NET 10 SDK and runs `dotnet test` without changing anything else. Which test platform runs the tests?
options: VSTest, until `global.json` opts in to Microsoft.Testing.Platform
Microsoft.Testing.Platform, which replaced VSTest as the .NET 10 default
Whichever platform the newest test package in the solution prefers
Neither, since `dotnet test` was removed in favor of `dotnet run`
explanation: From the .NET 10 SDK, `dotnet test` can run with Microsoft.Testing.Platform, but only when `global.json` sets `"test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" }`. VSTest is still the default. `dotnet run` also works for an xUnit v3 project because it is an executable, but `dotnet test` was not removed.
